facts: The three appellants in this appeal, namely, Ashok Kumar Chaudhary, Kailash Chaudhary and Baiju Chaudhary (hereinafter referred to as appellants A-1 to A-3 respectively) arrayed as accused Nos.1, 3 and 2 respectively in the charge-sheet, faced trial in Sessions Trial Case No.

The case of the prosecution in brief was that on 17th July, 1988 at about 6 p.m. the informant (PW-5) along with Bijoy Kumar Sanyal, Hardeo Chaudhary and Kishan Singh had gone to Dharampur Haat (Market) to make some purchases.
The motive of occurrence was given as previous enmity.

Fardbeyan of the informant was recorded by the A.S.I. of Pirbahore police station and was forwarded on the next day to the officer incharge of Bidupur police station within whose jurisdiction the occurrence had taken place.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet was submitted against the appellants under Sections 324, 307 read with S.34 Indian Penal Code, 1860.
issues: Whether the prosecution should have examined some independent witnesses to establish its case
Whether the evidence of PW-4 and PW-5 should be discarded as being closely related to the victim Ajay Kumar
petitioner_arguments: The incident having taken place at a public place in the evening, the prosecution ought to have examined some independent witnesses.
The evidence of PW-4 and PW-5 should be discarded as being closely related to the victim Ajay Kumar
There was an inordinate delay of five days in lodging the F.I.R., which is fatal to the prosecution case
respondent_arguments: Though it is true that the incident having taken place near the market around 6 p.m. on 17th July, 1988, the prosecution should have attempted to secure public witnesses who had witnessed the incident
The evidence of PW-4 and PW-5 is trustworthy and reliable
court_reasoning: One cannot lose sight of the ground realities that the members of the public are generally insensitive and reluctant to come forward to report and depose about the crime even though it is committed in their presence.
The relationship per se does not affect the credibility of a witness
A close relative would be the last to screen the real culprit and falsely implicate an innocent person
holding: The convictions are affirmed by the High Court, which has been upheld by this Court.
